skill.summary: Dispatch parallel agents for independent debugging tasks while preserving focused scopes and integration checks.

content.value_statement: Independent failures take too long when one agent investigates them one by one. This skill shows how to split work across focused Claude, Codex, or Claude Code agents and integrate results safely.
actual_capabilities: Explains when multiple failures are independent enough for parallel investigation.
Shows how to assign one focused agent per test file or subsystem.
Provides prompt structure for scoped agent debugging tasks.
Describes integration steps after agents return results.
Lists common mistakes that make parallel agent work ineffective.
limitations: Does not execute agent dispatch automatically by itself.
Works best when failures have clearly separate causes and files.
Requires a human or lead agent to review and integrate returned changes.
May create conflicts if agents edit overlapping code without isolation.

use_cases.title: Debug Separate Test Failures
use_cases.description: Assign different failing test files to separate agents so each investigation stays focused.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers maintaining large test suites

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Refactor Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Split unrelated regressions after a refactor into independent agent tasks with clear boundaries.

use_cases.title: Speed Up Triage Sessions
use_cases.description: Use parallel investigation to determine root causes across unrelated subsystems before integration.

prompt_templates.title: Check if Parallel Agents Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failures and tell me whether they are independent enough for parallel agent investigation. Group them by likely problem domain.

prompt_templates.title: Create Focused Agent Assignments
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these unrelated failures into separate agent tasks. Each task should include scope, goal, constraints, and expected return summary.

prompt_templates.title: Dispatch Independent Debugging Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Using Claude Code or another agent environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Dispatch one agent per independent failing test file. Tell each agent to fix only its assigned scope and report root cause plus changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Parallel Agent Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these agent summaries and changed files. Identify conflicts, verify the fixes work together, and recommend the safest integration order.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test files are failing after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends one agent per failing file, with each prompt limited to that file, its errors, and a root-cause summary.

output_examples.input: Agents returned fixes for separate subsystems.
output: Spot check for repeated agent mistakes.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether to parallelize exploratory debugging.
output_examples.output: The skill advises against parallel dispatch until the failures can be grouped into independent problem domains.

best_practices: Group failures by independent problem domain before dispatching agents.
Give each agent a narrow scope, explicit constraints, and expected output.
Review summaries, changed files, and full test results before integration.
anti_patterns: Do not dispatch parallel agents when one fix may affect all failures.
Do not give agents broad prompts such as fixing all tests at once.
Do not merge parallel changes without checking for conflicts and regressions.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when three or more failures are independent and can be investigated without shared context or shared state.

faq.question: Does this skill run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and prompt pattern for dispatching focused agents in tools that support agent tasks.

faq.question: Can I use it for related failures?
faq.answer: No. Related failures should be investigated together because one fix may change the diagnosis for the others.

faq.question: What should each agent receive?
faq.answer: Each agent should receive a specific scope, clear goal, constraints, relevant errors, and expected return format.

faq.question: How do I avoid conflicting changes?
faq.answer: Assign agents to separate files or subsystems, then review changed files before integrating their results.

faq.question: Which tools can use this workflow?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools for applying the parallel agent workflow.
